title: Ingress preflight and pin decision playbook for experimental open weights
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Intake of unvetted community weights into the model catalog creates operational and reliability risk. Current intake signals are inconsistent across teams and we lack a concise decision flow for when to pin a model version vs allow unpinned/ephemeral variants. This ticket clarifies requirements for an automated + reviewer-assisted preflight that produces a compatibility signal, a recommended pin decision, and a human-tractable rationale to be surfaced in the catalog entry.

Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable preflight and pin-decision playbook for new open-model submissions that balances safety, developer velocity, and runtime compatibility. Output must be a checklist and a machine-readable signal that the runtime and console can consume for onboarding and rollout automation.
scope_changes: IN: add a mandatory runtime preflight step for all community model submissions
IN: surface machine-readable compatibility grades in catalog metadata (compatible | partial | incompatible)
OUT: do not require full eval suite or long-term model scoring in scope for MVP
IN: require a short human rationale and pointer to weights provenance for all accepted entries
acceptance_criteria: A preflight script (language-agnostic shim) runs against submitted model artifacts and emits a standardized compatibility JSON with at least: model_architecture, tokenization_hint, kv_cache_compat, max_sequence_test_ok, perf_profile_sample
The catalog UI displays a concise compatibility badge (compatible | partial | incompatible) and the recommended pin state (pinned | unpinned | manual-review) with the preflight rationale
Runtime health probe accepts the compatibility JSON and refuses to schedule models marked 'incompatible' into the default hosted pool
A human reviewer can override the automated recommendation and the override is recorded in the catalog audit log with reason and reviewer id
Rollout gating: models recommended as 'partial' require canary rollout with specific latency and error thresholds before broad traffic; documented in onboarding checklist
Security review required boolean is set for models with external provenance flagged by preflight (e.g., unknown KMS, external license ambiguity)
decisions_log: 2025-02-21: PM/Runtime sync agreed to keep preflight lightweight for MVP and only emit compatibility signals; extensive evals deferred to 'post-ingest-evals' project
2025-02-24: Design requested clear UX language for compatibility badges to avoid unintuitive developer expectations; agreed to three-state badge
2025-02-27: Legal recommended a provenance pointer be mandatory on all external-weights submissions; accepted
2025-03-03: Engineering flagged that KV cache compatibility check must run locally in the preflight container to avoid false negatives in different infra; acceptance updated
notes_for_engineering: Preflight must be containerized and run in a hermetic sandbox (10 minute timeout)
Provide a minimal reference implementation (python + bash) that emits expected compatibility fields
Avoid heavy-weight model downloads in hosted preflight: use small sanity samples and metadata-only checks where possible
Pin recommendation logic: simple rule set for MVP — if any critical incompatibility then recommend 'pinned'; if all green recommend 'unpinned'; if mixed recommend 'manual-review'
qa_checklist: Verify preflight JSON schema against spec and sample models
Upload a known incompatible variant and confirm catalog marks 'incompatible' and blocks default scheduling
Simulate override by reviewer and check audit-log entry appears with reviewer name and reason
Confirm compatibility badge text and tooltip copy with design review
